page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a shared-core virtual machine instance belonging to the f1 server family. It features 1 vCPU mapped to a shared physical core on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor, with 1 thread per core. The instance is configured with 0.6 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 0.6 GB. It contains no local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the f1-micro operates in the lowest performance tier, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU scores of 384.79, placing it in the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory performance is similarly constrained, showing a cached read-only small block bandwidth of 80.8 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 0.2 GB/sec. Passmark testing yields a CPU score of 236.08 and a database operations score of 0.0, reflecting the limitations of the shared CPU allocation and minimal memory capacity. Static web serving throughput is measured at 0.22 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the f1-micro represents a low-resource entry point designed for minimal financial overhead rather than high-throughput compute density. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which can lead to resource contention and variable performance. Due to these hardware and benchmark constraints, the instance is suited for lightweight, non-production workloads such as basic development environments, simple cron jobs, low-traffic static web serving, or micro-services with minimal memory footprints.
